content.title: Comet C/2026 A1 (MAPS): Complete Information & Live Data | TheSkyLive
content.text: Below the horizon. Rise: 08:36 | Tran: 14:55 | Set: 21:12 Alt: -32.94° Az: 334.73° Direction: North-North-West Please note. This comet disintegrated during its perihelion passage on April 4, 2026, therefore it is not visible any more. The data shown on this page is provided just for reference, as if the comet survived its perihelion transit and continued along its orbit. C/2026 A1 (MAPS) disintegrated on April 4, 2026 during its perihelion transit. The following video shows the comet falling towards the Sun and the reappearance of its debris after the passage. Credits: SOHO/LASCO (ESA & NASA). Your browser does not support the video tag. Comet C/2026 A1 (MAPS) is in the constellation of Taurus, at a distance of 170,433,928.6 kilometers from Earth. The current Right Ascension is 03h 29m 28s and the Declination is +02° 42’ 27” (apparent coordinates). The estimated magnitude of comet C/2026 A1 (MAPS), computed using JPL Horizons's data, is 11.28. When available, please refer to the Observed Magnitude value and consider the Predicted Magnitude as a directional indication. Light Curve The following chart shows the light curve of comet C/2026 A1 (MAPS), i.e., its apparent magnitude as a function of time. The curve is calculated using the latest ephemerides provided by JPL Horizons. The magnitude data is sampled with the interval of 2 days. Because of this sampling, inaccuracies may occur for objects that have large variations of brightness over a few days. For comets, large discrepancies can arise between the calculated brightness and the observations due to their highly dynamic, and not always precisely predictable, behavior.
